description: This course is concerned with the dominant school of philosophy in late antiquity (200-600 AD),
a pivotal time in the history of philosophy that bridges the gap between ancient Greek and Roman
philosophy and medieval Jewish, Christian, and Islamic philosophy.  Herein we will study the
works of Plotinus, the so-called founder of  Neoplatonism, and three prominent Neoplatonists who
succeeded him, Porphyry, Iamblichus, and Proclus. Completion of Phil 235 or Greek 372 is
